The transport output proof remains open. The earlier optimized bounds were too wide
to convert from signed-log units back to flux. We tested whether changing the proof
graph could help, while preserving the saved model and its complete input box.

The new graph treats ELU directly. This activation is increasing and convex: a
tangent lies below it, and a line through an interval's endpoints lies above it.
The saturated part of each monotone head also has an equivalent expression whose
terms stay bounded. This changes the bound calculation while preserving the
network's predictions.

We checked the analytic relaxation and compared selected exports with JAX. The
proof runner also requires fresh random-box and held-out parity before each member
calculation. The focused validation is [40 focused checks pass in both normal and Tier A modes; lint, formatting and typing pass]{.claim}[C-269](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-269){.cid .st-measured}.

The pilot bounded one member per machine before considering a larger run:

| calculation | outcome |
|---|---|
| direct-ELU CROWN intersect interval propagation | [member 0 of each ensemble remains unknown; both processes complete in about 23 seconds, with physical inverse-transform overflow and looser intervals than the earlier optimized run]{.claim}[C-268](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-268){.cid .st-measured} |

Both processes finished and retained their training-space intervals, physical
conversion failures and source hashes. The intervals are looser than the preceding
optimized calculation. This is not a controlled comparison of graph representations:
the earlier run optimized its relaxation, while this pilot used fixed tangents.

We did not expand the unsuccessful pilot to the other members. A loose relaxation
is not a counterexample showing that the model reaches these extremes. It also
cannot supply a finite physical output domain to a guard.

V5 remains incomplete. Next comes improving intermediate activation intervals and
optimizing tangent choices before another small pilot. Transport local robustness
needs a certified full-box output range for its relative tolerance; EC robustness
and preparation of the EC reference comparison can proceed independently. The
MAST-U reference limitation and the final certification review remain open.
